cases.name: Alessia Maria Mesquita
cases.about: Her obituary said, "Alessia was a lifelong resident of New Haven. She graduated from East Haven Adult Education. She worked for many years at Home Depot until she decided she wanted to go into the medical field, and graduated from Branford Hall as a Medical Assistant. Alessia was employed as a medical assistant prior to her death. She absolutely loved her job and all her patients. Alessia loved, and was extremely proud of her Portuguese and Puerto Rican heritage. She always said, "she had the best of both worlds."
cases.narrative: He shot her about four times and killed her in broad daylight while she was standing outside of a parked car on Clifton St. in New Haven. Their one-year-old daughter was in the back seat.

cases.name: Destiny Sarah Rumley
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "She started her early education in the North Branford School system and then graduated from Wilbur Cross High School in 2022. Destiny attended Living Water Citadel of Hamden, CT under Overseer Jeanetta Beasley, where she gave her life to Christ at a young age.

During her childhood years, Destiny loved participating in church events, taking pictures that would last a lifetime and having sleepovers with her cousins. She mastered the art of braiding hair and showcasing her sense of style with her family, friends and of course on her self. She loved cooking and once she learned a new recipe you would often hear her saying

"taste this sis, yup good right." Destiny had a special way of bringing people together, whether at cookouts, parties or little get-togethers. Her heart was full of love for family and friends, and her beautiful smile and infectious laughter could light up any room. Many of her friendships began in childhood and continued throughout her young life. With her, friends became family with every memory, laugh and heart-to-heart conversation cherished.

Her caring and loving spirit flowed into her early career, leading her to become a sales associate at Walmart & Bowlero in Wallingford, amongst numerous other employments.

Destiny's greatest blessing was when she gave birth to her son, Ezekiel. The playfulness in her voice would echo through the front door as she called his name "Chujuupapi " He was her pride and joy, the center of her world. She was incredibly proud watching him grow. Her love for him was endless, unconditional, and knew no bounds. Her memory will live on through the laughter she inspired, the love she shared and the many hearts she touched along the way."
cases.narrative: He allegedly stabbed her nine times in front of her 3-year-old child.
